d: Every fleetd command and option, generated from the binary's own help.
x:
Generated from fleetd help , so it matches the binary this site was built with. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 failed (a check that did not pass), 2 usage, 3 refused, 4 hub or node unreachable, 78 ( listen ) the hub refused the key. fleetd version print the fleetd version and protocol fleetd help show this message fleetd update [--check] [--channel ] replace this fleetd with the latest release fleetd init [--yes] [--home ] [--listen ] [--url ] [--git-identity "Name "] [--no-service] [--unit-suffix ] set up fleetd step by step in a terminal: the hub on this machine (home default ~/.fleetd/hub, kept running by a systemd or launchd user service), where it listens (your tailnet when there is one), the claude and gh logins, the machines that run agents, a first project and the desktop app, then fleetd doctor. Run it again to check and repair; it keeps what works. --yes takes every default. Without a terminal and without --yes it only sets up the hub. --url is how devices reach the hub (default http://); --git-identity is the commit author for every machine (the GitHub noreply address for public repos); --no-service prepares everything but leaves starting the hub to you fleetd init --join --code [--machine-id ] [--git-identity "Name "] [--rejoin] make this machine a worker of that hub, without SSH from the hub: the command fleetd pair --worker prints on the hub. Run again, it keeps the node's enrolment and repairs the rest; --rejoin enrols again with a new code fleetd doctor [--home ] run every setup check on the hub now and print each problem with its fix fleetd uninstall [--home ] [--purge] stop and remove the hub's service; its data stays unless --purge, which also removes what an older fleetd installed for T3 Code fleetd machine add | --local [--machine-id ] [--tags a,b] [--dry-run] [--hub-url ] [--ssh-config ] [--home ] [--unit-suffix ] set up a machine that runs agents, over SSH (--local: this machine): copies this fleetd there, checks its claude (installed, version >=2.1.300, <2.2.0, logged in), enrolls the node and runs it as a user service, then waits until the machine is online; prints every command first, --dry-run only prints (for a fresh machine, without connecting); safe to run again fleetd machine remove [--purge] [--home ] stop and remove the node's service on the machine and revoke its key on the hub; --purge also deletes ~/.fleetd/node, ~/.fleetd/claude and ~/.fleetd/claude.env there, and what an older fleetd installed for T3 Code fleetd pair [--name ] [--home ] print a one-time code (15 min) that pairs the desktop app with this hub; the app on this machine pairs by itself fleetd pair --worker [--home ] print the one command that makes another machine a worker of this hub, with a one-time code (15 min): for a machine the hub can't reach over SSH fleetd hub start [--home ] [--listen ] [--queue-ttl ] [--router-model ] run the hub (default home ~/.fleetd/hub, listen 127.0.0.1:4790, writes to an offline machine wait 24 h, intents without a project are routed by the claude CLI with claude-haiku-5-5) fleetd hub key create --name --role --machines <'*'|id,id> [--home ] create an agent key for the MCP endpoint; prints the key once fleetd hub key create --human --name [--role ] [--machines <'*'|id,id>] [--home ] a key for a person's device (the desktop app): what it answers is recorded as the human's; role defaults to operate on every machine fleetd hub key list [--home ] fleetd hub key revoke [--home ] takes effect at once, also on a running hub fleetd hub token create --machine [--home ] print a one-time enrollment token (15 min) for `fleetd node join` fleetd node join --hub (--token | --token-file ) --machine [--tags a,b] [--name ] [--home ] [--enroll-only] enroll this machine with the hub, then keep its link up (node home default ~/.fleetd/node); --token-file - reads the token from stdin; --enroll-only exits once the hub has accepted this node fleetd node run [--home ] keep the link up for a machine that has joined fleetd listen --hub --key-file (--exec '' | --post ) [--types a,b] [--machines a,b] [--name ] deliver hub events, at least once and in order, to a command (one event's JSON on stdin) or a URL; the cursor lives in ~/.fleetd/listen/.cursor (name default "default"). Exits 78 when the hub refuses the key. fleetd retro run --hub --key-file [--window 14d] [--advise] run the retro now: one claude -p turn over the window's incidents (1-28 days) proposes playbook changes; --advise only suggests them fleetd brief create --workstream (--json '' | --file ) [--amend ] freeze the brief of a draft workstream and start it fleetd ask --key --class --text --rec [--options a,b] [--blocks ""] [--proceeded] [--workstream ] fleetd ask --kind do --key --class --text --step '' [--step '' ...] [--verify ''] a step is {"text","where":"|browser","command"?,"expect"?}; --verify is a cmd or http check fleetd runs once the human ticks it done (a failure reopens it) ask the human; answers already in the decision log come back at once fleetd ask --kind secret --key --sink env::|file:: [--env-name ] --text [--class credential] the human enters it in the desktop app, sealed to that machine; an env: sink writes the line = (N defaults to the key uppercased, . and - as _). You get its fingerprint, never the value fleetd gated run --class irreversible|money|credential --argv '' --reason [--cwd ] [--secret-env NAME= ...] [--timeout ] [--workstream ] a command the node runs exactly as stored, in the project workspace by default, only after a human approves it; secrets come from the node's own sinks. The result arrives in a wake fleetd ask withdraw [--use ] fleetd decide --key --value [--why ] [--scope project|workstream] [--workstream ] log a decision you made yourself fleetd status set "" [--workstream ] fleetd decisions search "" fleetd task spawn --workstream --title --prompt

[--kind write|read|review] [--areas a,b] [--model ] [--effort low|medium|high|max] [--tier S|M|L] [--estimate ] [--serves done:|issue:|defect:|ask:] [--pr ] [--qa] delegate work to a subagent; writers need --areas and --serves and get their own branch; a review task needs --pr, and --qa marks it a QA run fleetd task list [--state ] [--workstream ] fleetd task status fleetd task message "" steer a running task, answer a waiting one, or continue an ended one fleetd task cancel [--reason ] fleetd claim done --workstream fleetd runs the workstream's done-when checks itself; only all of them passing makes it done (exit 1 when a check did not pass) fleetd review verdict --task --sha --blocking --non-blocking --summary "" [--baseline --candidate ] the last step of a review task; a research judge also reports its metric for the baseline and the candidate, and fleetd computes GO, STOP or INCONCLUSIVE fleetd change enqueue --pr [--task ] [--workstream ] [--serves ] [--tier S|M|L] put a PR on its repo's merge train (a write task's PR goes on by itself); its body needs a 'Source: ' line. Only the train merges. fleetd change status fleetd inventory the project's open work ranked: failing checks, open issues (gh), open asks and TODO/FIXME markers; with nothing left that has a value source and no open child, the project's finish-all workstream goes idle fleetd workstream spawn --text "" --serves issue:<#n|url>|defect:|done: [--template bugfix|feature|research] a finish-all lead starts a child workstream for one item with a value source
